slot.brief: Flux through a coil changes from one value to another over a stated time interval (or a loop entering/leaving a field region); find the average induced emf using Faraday's law.

stem: The magnetic flux through each turn of a $20$-turn coil decreases uniformly from $8$ mWb to $2$ mWb in $0.03$ s. What is the magnitude of the average induced emf in the coil?
working:
$$|\mathcal{E}_{\rm avg}|=N\dfrac{|\Delta\Phi|}{\Delta t}=20\dfrac{(8-2)\times10^{-3}}{0.03}=4\ \text{V}$$

Independent check: Using Faraday’s law, \(\mathcal{E}=N|\Delta\Phi|/\Delta t=20(6\times10^{-3})/0.03=4\,\text{V}\).
solution:
By Faraday’s law, the magnitude of the average induced emf is
$$|\mathcal{E}_{\rm avg}|=N\frac{|\Delta\Phi|}{\Delta t}=20\frac{(8-2)\times10^{-3}}{0.03}=4\,\text{V}.$$
